title: TypeScript structural compatibility, interfaces, classes, and variance
concepts: A target type can accept a source value with the required members
Interfaces and classes describe instance and static shapes differently
Private and protected members affect compatibility through declaration origin
Function parameter variance has a method-syntax exception
Variance annotations document but do not arbitrarily redefine compatibility

inventory.title: Assignment compatibility and structural typing rules

sourceSnapshot.authority: Official TypeScript Handbook and release notes

accuracyFacts: Structural compatibility compares members rather than declaration names, except nominal-like behavior introduced by private/protected class members, enums, and other specific rules. TypeScript is intentionally not fully sound; do not promise that compatibility proves runtime safety.

Excess property checks are a special check for fresh object literals in certain contextual assignments, not a general exact-object or exact-interface rule. A previously stored variable may carry extra members and still be assignable structurally.

A class has separate static/constructor and instance sides. implements checks the instance side and does not change the class or create members; extends establishes runtime inheritance and static-member inheritance separately.

Private and protected class instance members affect compatibility only when they originate from the same declaration lineage. TypeScript private/protected access modifiers are distinct from ECMAScript # private elements, whose runtime semantics are covered in t06-018.
Index signatures require known properties to have compatible value types with the index signature. An index signature is not a guarantee that the runtime object contains every key.

strictFunctionTypes checks function-property parameters contravariantly, with a method/constructor parameter bivariance exception. Variance annotations do not override structural compatibility and must match structural use.

Multiple interface heritage must satisfy compatible inherited members; interfaces are open to declaration merging, but class declarations do not gain interface implementation behavior simply because their shapes overlap.
scopeExclusions: ECMAScript # private runtime semantics and JavaScript prototype inheritance (t06-018)
